findings.title: "Water now" spins forever when the request stalls (no timeout)
findings.steps: On /beds, make POST /api/waterings hang (browser_route that never responds), then click "Water now" for North bed and wait over 45 s.
findings.expected: The request times out after 10 s and an error is shown on the bed, after which the button works again.
findings.actual: The button still says "Watering…" and stays disabled indefinitely. The API client sets no timeout, and the past-watering "Saving…" button behaves the same way.
findings.evidence: About 45 s after clicking, the button text was 'Watering… North bed' with disabled=true, and no error was shown.

findings.title: Watering a second bed re-enables the first bed's button while its request is still pending, which allows duplicate waterings
findings.steps: Make POST for bed 1 hang. Click Water now on North bed, then click Water now on Shade corner (which succeeds).
findings.expected: North bed's button stays disabled until its own request finishes.
findings.actual: wateringBedId is a single shared ref. Shade corner's request resets it to null, so North bed's button is enabled again while its POST is still pending. Clicking it again records a second watering, and when the first request finishes it overwrites the other bed's notice.
findings.evidence: After the Shade request completed: 'Water now North bed disabled=false' while North's POST was still pending.

findings.title: Retrying a submit after a timeout or lost response creates a duplicate watering
findings.steps: Record a watering. The server commits it, but the response is lost or times out, so the user clicks again.
findings.actual: The request has no idempotency key and the server does no dedupe, so every retry inserts another row.
findings.evidence: Code: create_watering always INSERTs, and the client sends no request id.

findings.title: No retry button on the waterings page or the dashboard's Recent waterings when loading fails
findings.steps: Make /api/waterings* return 503, then use client-side navigation to Dashboard and to Waterings. Restore the API.
findings.expected: An error message with a Retry button that reloads the data without reloading the page.
findings.actual: Only 'Could not load recent waterings.' / 'Could not load waterings.' is shown, with no retry control. The dashboard doesn't even destructure refresh for waterings. The only way to recover is to reload the page, or on /waterings to change the filter.
findings.evidence: Page text in the error state contained only the alert, with no button.

findings.title: Bed filter fails silently when /api/beds fails
findings.expected: An error saying the beds could not be loaded, with a retry.
findings.actual: The Bed dropdown just contains 'All beds' and no error is shown, so the user can't filter and isn't told why. The beds error is never read.
findings.evidence: Options were ['All beds'] and no alert about beds appeared.

findings.title: Non-array (unexpected) waterings response crashes the page
findings.steps: Mock GET /api/waterings to return 200 {"items":[]}, then navigate to Waterings from Beds.
findings.actual: TypeError 'waterings.value?.reduce is not a function'. Navigation stalls: the URL is /waterings but Beds content is still shown, along with the Nuxt error overlay.
findings.evidence: The error overlay dialog showed 'TypeError waterings.value?.reduce is not a function'.

findings.title: Malformed watering fields are rendered as-is (e.g. 'x L', raw 'garbage' date, blank bed)
findings.actual: The row shows 'garbage', an empty bed cell, 'x L', and a delete label reading 'watering of ' with no bed name.
findings.evidence: Row text was 'garbage\t\tx L\tDelete watering of'.

findings.title: Server returns 500 for oversized integer ids
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error. SQLite overflows on an integer larger than 64 bits.
findings.evidence: curl returned 'Internal Server Error 500' for all three requests.

findings.title: Tiny litre amounts are accepted but displayed as '0 L'
findings.steps: Record a past watering with litres 0.001 (the form allows any value above 0; the API accepts it).
findings.expected: Either refuse amounts below the precision shown, or display them correctly.
findings.actual: The amount is saved and every list shows it as '0 L'.
findings.evidence: The dashboard and /waterings rows showed '1 Jan 2026 North bed 0 L'.

findings.title: Absurd past dates such as year 0001 are accepted
findings.expected: Refused with a visible reason, or limited to a sensible range.
findings.actual: It is saved and shown as '1 Jan 1' in the lists.
findings.evidence: API returned 201, and the UI rendered '1 Jan 1 North bed 1 L'.

findings.title: Bed filter gets out of sync with the URL
findings.steps: On /waterings?bed=2 (Shade corner), click the 'Waterings' nav link (or press browser Back to an unfiltered URL).
findings.actual: The URL becomes /waterings, but the dropdown stays on Shade corner and the list stays filtered. bedFilter is only read from route.query once and never watches the route.
findings.evidence: After the click, url=http://localhost:3791/waterings, select value=2, and only Shade corner rows were listed.

findings.title: Invalid ?bed= query shows a raw validation message
findings.expected: Ignore the bad filter, or show a friendly message with a way out.
findings.actual: The page shows 'Query.bed id: Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer', the dropdown shows 'All beds' while 'Clear filter' is visible, and there is no retry.

findings.title: Waterings table scrolls sideways at 375 px with a long bed name
findings.steps: Create a bed with a long name of 58 characters with no spaces (allowed by the API), record a watering for it, and open /waterings at 375 px wide.
findings.expected: No horizontal scrolling; long names wrap.
findings.actual: document scrollWidth is 511 px. The table overflows and the Delete column goes off-screen.
findings.evidence: With that bed, scrollWidth was 511; without it, 375.

findings.title: Retrying a delete after a timeout reports an error even though the delete happened
findings.steps: Delete a watering. The response is lost, so the user retries.
findings.expected: The retry is treated as success (the row is already gone).
findings.actual: The second DELETE gets a 404 and the page shows 'Watering not found.' as an error.
findings.evidence: Code: delete_watering raises not_found when the row is missing, and the client shows it in listError.

findings.title: Water now's date and time come from different clocks, and the future-date check uses the server's date
findings.steps: Use the app from a time zone ahead of the server's, near midnight.
findings.expected: Today's date is accepted, and 'now' entries are dated consistently with their time.
findings.actual: watered_on uses the server's local date while watered_at is UTC, and the client's max date is the browser's local date. A user ahead of the server is refused for 'today' with 'cannot be in the future', and 'now' entries can show a date that disagrees with their time and sort wrongly.
findings.evidence: Code: waterings.py now.astimezone().date() vs strftime of the UTC time; schemas.not_in_future uses date.today().
